text: GitMate 是面向 DSH Web 客户端的 Git 侧栏和 agent 工具集。它在右侧栏注册面板，并通过 Host 端共享实现提供 Git 操作。用户可以查看状态和差异、暂存与提交、管理分支和远程同步，也可让当前模型生成或优化提交说明、审阅暂存改动并拆分提交。适合在 DSH 会话中直接处理项目版本控制和代码变更审阅。需要本机可用的 Git；模型辅助功能使用会话默认模型。

GitMate adds a Git panel to the DSH web sidebar and provides agent tools for status, diffs, staging, commits, branches, and remote sync. It also uses the session model to generate commit messages, review staged changes, and suggest commit splits. Requires local Git.
想在 DSH 侧栏查看项目的 Git 改动并直接暂存和提交。
有没有办法让 agent 在会话里读取 Git 状态、分支和 diff？
我想根据暂存内容自动生成提交说明，也能补全我写的草稿。
提交前能不能让模型检查暂存改动并指出需要关注的地方？
想在 DSH 里管理分支、stash、标签以及远程同步。
I want to review diffs, stage changes, and commit without leaving my DSH session.
Can an agent inspect Git status and manage branches or remotes for my workspace?
Help me generate a commit message and review staged changes before I commit.
GitMate 的功能「Git 面板中的仓库操作」：查看状态和差异，暂存、取消暂存或丢弃改动，并创建或修订提交。 可通过侧栏面板或相应 agent 工具触发，输入为当前会话仓库及操作参数，结果显示在面板或工具响应中。
GitMate 的功能「模型辅助提交说明」：依据暂存 diff 生成提交说明，也可在用户草稿基础上优化；语言和格式可配置。 可通过侧栏面板或相应 agent 工具触发，输入为当前会话仓库及操作参数，结果显示在面板或工具响应中。
GitMate 的功能「暂存改动审阅与拆分」：让模型审阅暂存改动并给出发现，或提出按意图拆分提交的方案。 可通过侧栏面板或相应 agent 工具触发，输入为当前会话仓库及操作参数，结果显示在面板或工具响应中。
GitMate 的功能「分支、历史和远程工作流」：查看提交历史，切换或合并分支，并执行 fetch、pull、push 或同步。 可通过侧栏面板或相应 agent 工具触发，输入为当前会话仓库及操作参数，结果显示在面板或工具响应中。
dsh-gitmate 提供工具 git_status：Read repository status, branch, staged, modified, untracked, and conflicted files.
dsh-gitmate 提供工具 git_diff：Read diffs for staged, unstaged, or untracked changes.
dsh-gitmate 提供工具 git_stage：Stage, unstage, or discard selected changes.
dsh-gitmate 提供工具 git_commit：Create or amend a commit, optionally generating a message and pushing.
dsh-gitmate 提供工具 git_reset：Undo the latest commit with a selected reset mode.
dsh-gitmate 提供工具 git_log：Read commit history.
dsh-gitmate 提供工具 git_init：Initialize a repository and optionally create initial files.
dsh-gitmate 提供工具 git_config：Read or change Git configuration.
dsh-gitmate 提供工具 git_sync：Fetch, pull, push, or sync with a remote.
dsh-gitmate 提供工具 git_branch：List, switch, create, delete, or merge branches.
dsh-gitmate 提供工具 git_stash：Save, restore, inspect, or drop stashes.
dsh-gitmate 提供工具 git_tag：List, create, or delete tags.
dsh-gitmate 提供工具 git_revert：Create a new commit that reverses a selected commit.
dsh-gitmate 提供工具 git_cherry_pick：Apply selected commits.
dsh-gitmate 提供工具 git_rebase：Replay commits onto another branch or revision.

dsh-gitmate README · GitMate：**A Git panel in the [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) sidebar — plus the same operations as fifteen agent tools.**

Runs anywhere the Harness does: macOS, Linux, and Windows (PowerShell).

dsh-gitmate README · GitMate：Only two things genuinely differ across platforms, and both live on the Host side: **how arguments are quoted** (PowerShell doubles a single quote, a POSIX shell closes-escapes-reopens; chosen by `process.platform`) and **how the environment is passed** (through the shell request's `env` field rather than a POSIX `VAR=value` prefix, which is not a command on Windows). Nothing else is platform-aware: paths go through `node:path`, nothing outside `lib/` is written, and no file needing an executable bit is created. When the sandbox will not start, the advice **names the cause for the platform you are on** (bubblewrap/Landlock on Linux, `sandbox-exec` on macOS, `%TEMP%` on Windows).

dsh-gitmate README · GitMate：English | [中文](README.zh.md)

Review changes, read diffs, stage, commit with a generated message, merge, stash, sync, and rewind history without leaving the panel. Every operation is also a tool the agent can call, so asking in chat works too.

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:alanhaskey/dsh-gitmate
```

Restart DSH once, refresh the page, then open **GitMate** from the sidebar's **+** menu.

dsh-gitmate README · GitMate：> The internal ids (Loader row `dsh-git`, tab key) differ from the package name on purpose: the row id is the key of a config row you may already have, and renaming it would orphan your saved settings.

dsh-gitmate README · Reviewing and committing：- **Four groups** — conflicts, staged, changes, untracked. Each row shows the kind in words, the path, and that file's `+N −M`. Row actions stage, unstage, and discard, with a second click for anything destructive.
- **Diffs like an editor** — two line-number gutters, `+`/`−` markers, tinted rows, and only the changed span of a replaced line marked. Click a file to expand it in place; click again to collapse. Widen the context from 3 lines to 24 when a hunk needs more of the file.
- **One row of list actions**, shown only when they would do something, with the counts in the labels.
- **Amend** — fold the staged changes into the previous commit; leaving the message box empty keeps the existing message.
- **A draggable splitter** between the list and the commit card resizes the message box.
- **A panel that is working says so** — every operation shows a turning indicator and names itself ("Committing…", "Reviewing the staged changes…") instead of only greying its buttons out. It sits with the messages at the foot of the list, above the splitter, so it never covers the commit box.

dsh-gitmate README · AI features：| Feature | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Commit message** | Generated from the staged diff. If you have already typed something, the button becomes *Refine draft*: the model keeps your intent and fills in the rest instead of replacing it. |
| **Review before commit** | Reads the staged changes and reports only what would bite — a wrong result, a missed edge case, an unhandled error, a committed secret, debug output left in, a behaviour change with no test. Click a finding to open that file's diff. |
| **Split this commit** | Divides the staged changes into commits that each stand on their own, with a message for each. The plan is a draft you can edit: rewrite any message, merge a group into the one above, remove one, ask for a new plan, commit one group at a time, or commit them all in order. Each commit leaves the other files staged. |
| **Explain a change** | Two to five bullets on what a file's change does, so you can review without reading every line. |
| **Image and PDF preview** | Images and PDFs have no patch to read — git reports them as binary — so opening one reads the **current working-tree file** and shows it: `png`/`jpg`/`jpeg`/`gif
dsh-gitmate README · AI features：Buttons that call a model are marked **AI**. Every generation uses the session's default model — there is no second model to configure.

dsh-gitmate README · Branches, history, remotes：- **Branch selector** — switch, create, delete, and merge any branch into the checked-out one. A conflicted merge is reported with the files that need a decision, and can be aborted.
- **Commit graph** — every branch and remote-tracking branch, not just this one. Strokes are computed on the Host and shipped with the data, so "the rows join up" is an assertion rather than something to eyeball. Two things make it hold:

dsh-gitmate README · Branches, history, remotes：- **The straight runs are elements pinned to the row's bottom**, not coordinates inside a fixed-height box. A row's height is not fixed — expanding a commit makes it much taller — and a fixed box left a gap between every pair of rows, which is what made the tree look like it was floating.
- **When several lanes wait for the same commit, all but the claimed one are released.** Otherwise they keep waiting for a commit already emitted and drag a line to the bottom with no commit on it — the other half of the floating look.

dsh-gitmate README · Branches, history, remotes：A branch opening here starts **below** the node and one converging here arrives **above** it, each joined to the node by a curve; one hue carries three weights — the commit's own line, the branch curves, and the lanes merely passing through. Expand a commit for its full message, the files it touched, and what you can do to it: rewind, revert, cherry-pick, rebase, or tag. Click a changed file to see its diff inside that commit.
- **Remotes** — push, pull, fetch, and a **Sync** that fetches, fast-forwards, then pushes. It refuses to merge a diverged branch rather than inventing a merge commit.
- **Stash** — set work aside and take it back later (pop, apply, drop).

dsh-gitmate README · A directory holding several repositories：A workspace root is often just a **container for several projects** — not a repository itself, with `alpha/` and `beta/` below it. Asking "is this a repository" answers "no" for every one of them, so the panel used to offer only to initialise a new one.

dsh-gitmate README · A directory holding several repositories：The panel now **finds the repositories under that root** (three levels deep, skipping `node_modules`/`vendor`/`dist` and the like, at most forty), lists them, and works on the one you pick. A chip in the header takes you back to the list. **When the root is itself a repository it lists only itself**, so nested submodules are not offered as separate projects.

dsh-gitmate README · A directory holding several repositories：The boundary: the panel only accepts a path **inside the session's directory** — `/etc`, or anything that climbs out with `../..`, is ignored and the session's own folder is used instead. The agent tools work the same way: point one at a subdirectory and git finds the repository root by itself.

dsh-gitmate README · Setup：Without a repository the **history button is disabled** — there is no history to show — while **settings stays reachable**, because that is where someone looks when the panel is not doing what they expect. If the repository disappears while the panel is open (the folder changed, `.git` was removed), the view falls back to the change list rather than leaving the button lit on a view that cannot render.

dsh-gitmate README · Setup：One click initialises a repository and writes the local commit identity; two buttons handle `.gitignore`. Nothing is chosen from a list of ecosystems — the plugin reads the project and decides.

dsh-gitmate README · Configuration：Settings live in this plugin's own row in `cordis.patch.yml`, so they survive upgrades and stay visible on the Plugins page. Everything below is a button or a checkbox; there is nothing to type unless you want custom instructions.

dsh-gitmate README · Configuration：| Key | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `messageLanguage` | `auto` | Language of generated text: `auto` (follow the repository), `en`, `zh`. When unset or `auto`, the panel's own messages read as Chinese. |
| `messageStyle` | `conventional` | `conventional` (`feat: …`) or `plain`. |
| `messageTemplate` | — | Extra instructions, appended last so they override the defaults. |
| `signoff` | `false` | Add a `Signed-off-by` trailer. |
| `defaultBranch` | `main` | Branch created by *Initialise*. |
| `maxPromptBytes` | `24000` | Diff text handed to the model per change set. |
| `maxDiffBytes` | `80000` | Patch text a tool returns before truncating. |
| `commandTimeoutMs` | `60000` | Per git command; network commands get four times this. |

dsh-gitmate README · Safety：- **Nothing destructive happens on a single click.** Discarding, deleting a branch, dropping a stash, rebasing, and rewinding all ask first, and say what will be lost.
- **Rewinding and reverting are separate**, because they are: rewinding moves the branch and rewrites history, reverting adds an inverse commit and is safe for anything already pushed. The panel warns before a rewind that would rewrite published history.
- **"Undo this commit" and "rewind to here" are separate too.** On the newest commit the button undoes that commit and leaves its changes staged, unstaged, or deleted as you choose; on an older commit it moves the branch pointer back to that commit. The notice names the commit that was actually undone and always states how many were discarded — including none.
- **A refusal says which mode refused.** A read-only session cannot write `.git`, so committing and switching branches are rejected by design; the message names the mode and what to switch to. If it is already `danger-full-access` and still refused, the sandbox backend on that machine is refusing writes and the Harness needs restarting — two different problems, told apart.

lib/impl.js        operations + the fifteen agent tools

dsh-gitmate README · Development：The bundle has no dependencies at all — nothing to install, nothing to duplicate inside the profile. `lib/client.js` is hand-written, so a change to it needs only a page refresh; a change to the Host half needs the bundle reloaded.
